Crew-13 Ultra-Fast Transit
uploads.title: Slamming Brakes at 17,500 MPH #Shorts
facts: To catch the space station faster, the spacecraft does not fly directly toward it; it must launch into a lower, dangerous orbit to let Earth's gravity fling it forward, essentially falling downward to speed up.

A faster transit is physically more punishing: it compresses 'Space Adaptation Syndrome'—where fluid rushes to the head and causes severe nausea—into a tight window, forcing astronauts to perform delicate docking maneuvers while actively fighting debilitating motion sickness.

While the capsule screams through orbit at 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h) relative to Earth, the final physical docking must occur at a relative speed slower than a crawling baby—just 0.1 miles per hour—demanding absolute stillness while hurtling through a vacuum.

facts: Carved top-down from a single solid basalt cliff; a single mistake would ruin the entire 100-foot multi-level structure.
Modern excavation engineers calculate 400,000 tons of volcanic rock were removed, yet zero debris was found anywhere in a 50km radius.

uploads.title: Kailash Mandir Ka 4 Lakh Ton Raaz 🏛️ #Shorts #Mystery
facts: Among 70 massive carved stone pillars at Veerabhadra Temple, one pillar does not touch the granite floor.
A British engineer tried to shift it using heavy iron levers, but the entire temple ceiling shifted, proving it is a seismic load-bearing balance lock.
Ancient Vijayanagara builders engineered floating micro-cantilever joints that absorb earthquake shockwaves.
